questions.q:
With reference to the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. Legal and medical education are brought under the new Commission.
2. The apex Commission will not control funding.
3. Appeals against the Regulatory Council's penalties lie before the Supreme Court.
4. The Bill seeks to repeal the UGC Act, the AICTE Act and the NCTE Act.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 4 are correct: funding is kept away from the regulator, and three older laws would go. Statement 1 is wrong, since legal and medical education stay under separate Acts. Statement 3 is wrong, as appeals lie before the Central Government, which has been a point of debate about autonomy. The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha and referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.

questions.q:
As of mid-2025, which of the following countries had been certified malaria-free by the WHO?
1. Georgia
2. Sri Lanka
3. Cabo Verde
4. India
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Georgia was certified in 2025, Cabo Verde in 2024 and Sri Lanka in 2016, so the first three qualify. India is not certified, being on the path towards zero indigenous cases by 2030 under its national framework. China and Egypt are other recent additions. The presence of neighbours on this list is important, because malaria crossing borders remains a real challenge once domestic transmission declines.

questions.q:
In the context of malaria elimination, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Plasmodium vivax infection needs a 14-day radical treatment.
Statement-II: Plasmodium vivax can stay dormant in the liver and cause relapses.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and the second explains the first. Vivax forms dormant liver stages called hypnozoites, which can reactivate weeks or months later, so treating blood-stage parasites alone leaves infection behind. Long radical treatment targets these stages. That is why vivax, which makes up nearly two-thirds of cases in the region, complicates elimination: people seeming cured can relapse and restart transmission, especially if they do not finish the course.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 17-19; hypnozoite biology is static

questions.q: For WHO certification of malaria-free status, a country must have
o: interrupted local transmission of Plasmodium falciparum and P. vivax for at least three consecutive years, irrespective of its surveillance system
reported zero indigenous cases for at least one year, with an Annual Parasite Incidence below one in every district
achieved a 75 per cent fall in cases against its 2015 level
interrupted local transmission of all human malaria parasites for at least three consecutive years, with a functioning surveillance system
questions.e: Certification needs both a three-year record of no local transmission of all human malaria parasites and a system able to prevent re-establishment. So a two-species record without surveillance falls short, and one year of zero cases is too brief, since incidence below one is only a programme milestone. A 75 per cent reduction is a target under WHO's Global Technical Strategy. Sri Lanka and China were certified under this standard.

questions.q:
With reference to malaria data in India, consider the following statements:
1. Annual Parasite Incidence means confirmed new cases in a year per 1,000 people under surveillance.
2. In 2023, Tripura and Mizoram were the exceptions with an Annual Parasite Incidence above one.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Annual Parasite Incidence scales cases to the population watched, allowing comparison between States of different sizes. Thirty-four States and UTs were below one in 2023, and the two high readings came from the North-East, where forested terrain and border movement complicate control. District-level analysis is now used to sharpen action in high-burden pockets, including 160 districts with zero indigenous cases.

questions.q:
In Amit Kumar v. Union of India, on student suicides in higher educational institutions, the Supreme Court:
1. invoked Article 142 of the Constitution.
2. contemplated well-being audits, whose scores may be linked to NAAC grading.
3. asked that any suicide or unnatural death of a student be reported to the police immediately.
4. directed that vacant faculty and administrative posts be filled within a set period.
How many of the above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. Article 142 lets the Court do complete justice where gaps exist. Linking audits to accreditation gives institutions a reason to take well-being seriously. The reporting duty applies whether the death occurs on campus, in a hostel or in private accommodation. Filling posts addresses the staff shortages behind weak support. The directions also cover pending scholarships and separate NCRB data for students in higher education.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill rests on Entry 66 of the Union List.
Statement-II: 'Education' is a subject in the Concurrent List.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but the second does not explain the first. Entry 66 gives the Union power to coordinate and determine standards in higher education, research and technical institutions, and that is the Bill's specific basis. Concurrent status of education would allow State laws as well, and that is the reason federal concerns have been raised about a single regulator. So Statement-II explains the debate and not the legislative source.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 80-81; Entry 25, Concurrent List is static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Initiative : Menstrual hygiene component
1. National Guidelines on MHM : Issued under the National Health Mission for urban slums
2. Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana : 'Suvidha' oxo-biodegradable napkins
3. Samagra Shiksha : Vending machines and incinerators in schools
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 2 and 3 are correct. Janaushadhi Kendras sell low-priced Suvidha pads, while Samagra Shiksha addresses access and disposal at school. Pair 1 is wrong: the National Guidelines on Menstrual Hygiene Management were issued under the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan for awareness in rural areas. The range of schemes shows the issue spans health, education and sanitation, and it has been handled across several ministries.

questions.q:
With reference to accreditation of higher education in India, consider the following statements:
1. The National Assessment and Accreditation Council functions under the AICTE Act and accredits specific programmes.
2. The National Board of Accreditation was set up by the UGC and accredits whole institutions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct, since the two have been swapped. NAAC was set up by the UGC and assesses institutions as a whole. The National Board of Accreditation is linked to the AICTE framework and looks at particular programmes, for example B.Tech Mechanical. The VBSA Bill would move accreditation to a dedicated council. Well-being audits under the Amit Kumar directions may also feed into NAAC grading.

questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's reasoning in its menstrual health judgment, consider the following pairs:
Provision : Use in the reasoning
1. Section 3 of the RTE Act : Separate toilets for boys and girls as a norm
2. Article 14 : Substantive equality, as identical treatment can perpetuate exclusion
3. Article 21A : Inaccessible sanitary products affect the right to education
4. Section 19 of the RTE Act : Free education means removing all financial barriers
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 2 and 3 are correct. The Court said that treating unequal situations alike can turn biology into structural exclusion, and tied lack of products to the right to education. Pairs 1 and 4 are swapped: Section 3 was read to mean free education removes all barriers beyond fees, while Section 19 contains norms such as separate toilets. Together these made the absence of facilities a constitutional failure.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 83; Shankar IAS pp. 19-21

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about challenges to malaria elimination:
1. WHO has reported partial artemisinin resistance in several African countries.
2. Malaria transmission in Indian cities is linked only to breeding in sewage and polluted drains.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: partial resistance to artemisinin, with partner drugs also weakening, is a warning for global treatment. Statement 2 is wrong: urban malaria is linked to construction sites and to clean water stored in apartments, so household-level action is needed along with government measures. This is why the way ahead includes joint government-household effort, and also mandatory reporting from private practitioners.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's directions on menstrual hygiene in schools:
1. Free sanitary napkins are to be provided in government schools, with private schools outside the direction.
2. MHM corners are to keep spare innerwear, spare uniforms and disposable bags.
3. District Education Officers are to inspect schools and gather anonymous student feedback.
4. Boys are also to be educated about menstruation.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Practical support at school, regular monitoring and attention to stigma among male pupils and teachers all form part of the directions. Statement 1 is wrong: the direction covers all schools, government and private alike, which makes the ruling much wider than a welfare measure. The aim is that menstruation should not cause absence or dropout in Classes 6 to 12.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 83; Shankar IAS p. 20

questions.q: The 'orange economy', mentioned in the context of India's youth, refers to
o: industries classified in the 'orange' category for pollution
economic activity in citrus-growing and horticulture belts
informal work in sectors at moderate risk of automation
the part of the economy based on creative and cultural output
questions.e: The orange economy means the creative economy, including areas such as animation, and it is cited as a source of exports and jobs for young people. The horticulture idea is a guess from the colour. The word has no link to automation risk. CPCB's Orange category is a pollution class and is unrelated, even though colour labels might confuse a careless reader. Sindhuja Rajamaran's animation work is cited as an example.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Initiative : Feature or nodal body
1. YUVAi : AI solutions by school students, through MeitY and the National e-Governance Division
2. Startup India : Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
3. Kashi Declaration : Global standard on the ethical use of AI
4. Model Youth Gram Sabha : Simulated meetings that teach Panchayati Raj processes
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct. YUVAi targets Classes 8 to 12 across eight thematic sectors. Startup India provides mentorship, incubation and collateral-free loans through DPIIT. Model Youth Gram Sabhas give young people practical civic learning. Pair 3 is wrong: the Kashi Declaration relates to a drug-free campaign, listed alongside Fit India under well-being. It has nothing to do with artificial intelligence, despite the AI-themed initiatives around it.

questions.q:
With reference to malaria elimination in India, consider the following statements:
1. The National Framework for Malaria Elimination targets zero indigenous cases by 2030.
2. The National Strategic Plan 2023-27 treats surveillance as a core intervention.
3. The World Malaria Report 2025 records India's exit from the 'High Burden to High Impact' group.
4. An interim milestone seeks to interrupt indigenous transmission nationwide by 2027.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. The Framework sets the long-term goal, and the Strategic Plan puts it into operation through 'test, treat and track'. Exit from the high-burden group in 2024 reflects a large decline in cases since 2015. The 2027 milestone matters because WHO certification depends on three consecutive years without local transmission, so the 2030 target needs transmission stopped well before then.

questions.q:
Under the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025, match the Parishad with its function:
List-I
A. Viniyaman Parishad
B. Gunvatta Parishad
C. Manak Parishad
List-II
1. Academic standards
2. Regulation
3. Accreditation
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Bill creates an apex Commission with three separate councils. Viniyaman, meaning regulation, handles regulatory matters. Gunvatta, meaning quality, handles accreditation. Manak, meaning standard, sets academic standards. The Hindi words themselves are useful clues. Separating these functions is meant to reduce the overlaps and conflicts seen in the older arrangement, where bodies such as the UGC combined several roles in one institution.

questions.q:
With reference to Tamil Nadu's malaria categories, consider the following statements:
1. Category I districts, including Chennai, are in the elimination phase.
2. Category O districts are those where intensified control of high transmission is under way.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: five districts, including Chennai, form Category I, with incidence below one per thousand. Statement 2 is wrong: Category O means prevention of re-establishment, covering the larger group of districts with zero indigenous cases. The labels sound as if they mean the reverse, which is the trap. The State's work includes larval control, intensive testing and surveillance of migrant workers from malaria-prone States.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'demographic winter':
1. Replacement-level fertility is generally taken as a total fertility rate of about 2.1.
2. An inverted population pyramid has a wide young base and a narrow elderly top.
3. The phenomenon is confined to developed countries.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct: below about 2.1 births per woman, a population eventually shrinks without migration. Statement 2 is wrong: an inverted pyramid has a narrow young base and a wide elderly top, so fewer young people support more elderly. Statement 3 is wrong: this is no longer a problem for rich nations alone, as China's continuing decline shows. Causes include urban costs, delayed marriage and legacy policies.
